audit_findings.title: The bridge may treat operating and expansion cash as entirely surplus
audit_findings.magnitude: $435.599m bridge exposure ($3.65/share; 37.6% of the $1,158m base equity value); required reserve unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: The bridge adds cash and short-term investments to operating value; any required operating or growth cash is not distributable excess cash and should be excluded from the bridge.
audit_findings.evidence: We believe that cash provided by operating activities and existing cash on hand, together with amounts available under our 2022 Credit Facility, will be sufficient to satisfy our anticipated cash requirements for the next twelve months and foreseeable future, including our expected capital expenditures for expansion of our CAVA restaurant base, operating lease obligations, and other working capital obligations.
audit_findings.explanation: The full cash addition is demonstrated, but the amount required for liquidity and committed expansion is unresolved. Removing even a substantial portion would materially reduce intrinsic value and the buy-below price, although it would not reverse the conclusion that $60.76 is above the modeled value range.
audit_findings.action: Quantify minimum operating liquidity and cash committed to signed restaurant, manufacturing, technology, lease and working-capital programs, then rerun the bridge using only distributable excess cash.

audit_findings.title: Forecast growth may be valued without its required reinvestment
audit_findings.magnitude: $85.038m FY2025 capex above D&A ($158.699m less $73.661m), equal to 165.4% of the $51.4m anchor; valuation adjustment unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Owner earnings must deduct maintenance capital, while the growth forecast must retain or deduct the incremental restaurant, technology and manufacturing investment required to produce that growth.
audit_findings.evidence: Total capital expenditures for fiscal 2026 are expected to be higher than fiscal 2025.
audit_findings.explanation: The large capex requirement and positive-growth forecasts are demonstrated, but the record does not establish how the $51.4m anchor divided maintenance from expansion capital or how forecast reinvestment was charged. Because the observed capex-minus-D&A amount exceeds the anchor, an omitted reinvestment requirement is reasonably capable of materially reducing operating value.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile the anchor to total capex, capitalized payroll and accrued capital purchases; estimate maintenance and growth capital separately; and rerun each scenario with explicit reinvestment sufficient to fund its growth.

audit_findings.title: The anchor contains an unusually favorable tax rate tied to equity awards
audit_findings.magnitude: $9.543m FY2025 tax benefit, equal to 18.6% of the $51.4m anchor; sustainable-tax adjustment unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: The unusually low cash-tax burden increases the owner-earnings anchor, which is then grown and capitalized throughout the DCF.
audit_findings.evidence: The effective income tax rate for fiscal 2025 was 10.0%, which includes the permanent benefit associated with the vesting of restricted stock units (“RSUs”) and exercise of stock options above grant date fair values.
audit_findings.explanation: The FY2025 benefit and 10.0% effective tax rate are demonstrated. The July 2026 filing reports a 23.2% year-to-date effective rate while still recognizing a $4.214m equity-award benefit, showing that both normalized taxes and recurring award benefits require modeling. Perpetuating the FY2025 benefit without a sustainable-tax analysis could materially overstate operating value.
audit_findings.action: Build a cash-tax schedule covering NOL balances, the 80% limitation, expected equity-award deductions and the post-NOL tax rate, then rerun the DCF with normalized annual taxes.

audit_findings.title: Signed but uncommenced leases may escape both the bridge and current earnings
audit_findings.magnitude: $146.5m of undiscounted signed, uncommenced lease payments at FY2025 year-end; July 2026 residual and valuation effect unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: The commitments can affect growth through future rent, pre-opening costs, capital expenditure and ramp losses, while the associated restaurants can add revenue and owner earnings; they are not automatically a debt deduction.
audit_findings.evidence: As of December 28, 2025, future minimum lease payments excluded $ 146.5 million relating to legally binding leases executed but not yet commenced.
audit_findings.explanation: The FY2025 commitment is demonstrated, but the latest filing does not separately identify how much remained uncommenced or map the leases to modeled openings. The value direction depends on whether the forecast includes both the costs and the restaurant economics. The gross commitment is large, but it is not a measure of lost equity value, so materiality cannot be established from the present record.
audit_findings.action: Trace every FY2025 uncommenced lease into the July 2026 recognized lease balance and opening pipeline, then model its rent, capex, pre-opening expense, ramp losses and revenue; separately value abandoned or uneconomic sites.

audit_findings.title: The convertible note may be treated inconsistently between earnings and the bridge
audit_findings.magnitude: $10.715m July 2026 note fair value ($0.09/share; 0.9% of the $1,158m base equity value), plus $0.291m FY2025 and $0.424m 2026 year-to-date unrealized gains
audit_findings.mechanism: Omitting a non-operating note from the bridge understates value, while retaining its unrealized fair-value gains in recurring owner earnings overstates operating value.
audit_findings.evidence: As of December 28, 2025, the Company’s estimated fair value of the Note Receivable was $ 5.3 million.
audit_findings.explanation: The July 2026 filing demonstrates that both $5m investments were funded and the note was worth $10.715m. Even complete omission equals only about 0.9% of base equity value, and the FY2025 gain equals about 0.6% of the anchor. The inconsistent classification should be corrected but cannot materially change the valuation conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Confirm whether the anchor purged the $0.291m gain, classify the note consistently as an operating asset or separate investment, and add its latest fair value to the bridge only if excluded from operating value.

audit_findings.title: A one-time executive separation cost may remain in the anchor
audit_findings.magnitude: $0.832m, equal to 1.6% of the $51.4m anchor; a full proportional add-back implies about $11.7m or $0.10/share, approximately 1.0% of base equity value before tax effects
audit_findings.mechanism: If retained in normalized owner earnings, the event-specific expense lowers the anchor and therefore lowers forecast operating value.
audit_findings.evidence: Includes costs associated with the separation of the Company’s Chief Operations Officer.
audit_findings.explanation: Even treating the entire cost as nonrecurring produces only about a 1% change in base equity value. The July 2026 filing also reports another $0.545m of executive transition costs, so recurring management-transition expense may warrant retention. Either treatment is too small to alter the valuation conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Verify the $0.832m treatment in the anchor, compare executive-transition costs across several years, and make a consistent normalization adjustment only if such costs are demonstrably nonrecurring.
